title: Chapter 44
content:
Jakyeong drifted off in the backseat on the drive back to the estate. He had planned to leave immediately after concluding his brief exchange with Chairman Kang, but Kang Seok-joo had cornered him on his way out, stalling him for quite a while. Seok-joo kept lamenting Choi Ki-tae's death with theatrical sorrow, though he seemed far more heartbroken over the prospect of losing the capital he’d invested in the man's venture.

Rolling down the dark mountain road beneath sparse, buzzing streetlamps, the pitch-black forest felt thick enough for anything to leap out from the shadows. The gathering storm only deepened the gloomy atmosphere. A flash of lightning cleaved the dark sky, followed moments later by a low, earth-shaking rumble of thunder.

As the car pulled up to the estate's main gates, someone was standing by the entrance holding a large black umbrella. Park Tae-soo? Jakyeong reached for the door handle, then paused.

It was Kang Il-hyun.

Watching him approach through the sheets of rain gave Jakyeong a strange, unsettled feeling. He's not waiting on a toddler—why stand out in the storm?

The moment the car door swung open, Il-hyun angled the umbrella overhead, offering a gentle smile. "It's pouring quite heavily."

Jakyeong stepped out and headed toward the front doors. Tilting the canopy to shield Jakyeong against the wind-driven rain left Il-hyun's right shoulder completely drenched. Once inside the foyer, Jakyeong reached up and brushed the heavy droplets from the man's soaked jacket with a deadpan face.

Il-hyun beamed, looking entirely too pleased with the gesture. "How attentive."

Choosing not to dignify that with a response, Jakyeong headed up the grand staircase. When he realized Il-hyun was trailing close behind—looking ready to follow him straight into the bedroom—Jakyeong pivoted sharply at the threshold, blocking the doorway.

"I'm exhausted, Director Kang. If you have something to say, say it here."

Il-hyun stepped in close, leaning his face in to catch a breath. "Did you drink over there?"

"No."

"What did the two of you discuss?"

Without a word, Jakyeong unbuckled the luxury timepiece from his wrist and offered it out. When Il-hyun didn't take it, Jakyeong grabbed the man's hand and pressed the watch firmly into his palm.

"You listened to the entire conversation. Why play dumb now?"

Il-hyun tilted his head slightly, prompting Jakyeong to gesture toward the watch casing once more.

A slow, wicked smile curled the corners of Il-hyun's lips. "Ah. You found it."

"Is it a new prototype? It didn't trigger a single security scanner when I passed through the Chairman's gates."

Jakyeong had wondered why the man had suddenly slapped an eight-figure watch on his wrist. Suspicious, he had pried the caseback open during the car ride over, discovering a covert audio transmitter embedded beneath the movement. Slightly larger than a grain of rice, the micro-chip was state-of-the-art—completely undetected by high-end frequency sweeps.

Truth be told, Jakyeong was far more covetous of the cutting-edge bug than the luxury watch itself.

"Did you plant one in my room, too?" Jakyeong asked, narrowing his eyes.

Il-hyun frowned in mock offense. "No. That transmitter only arrived yesterday."

Hard to believe a word out of his mouth. Jakyeong resolved to tear his suite and en-suite bath apart the moment he found a free window.

"If you like it, should I source a few for you?"

"I certainly wouldn't turn them down."

Free tactical gear was always welcome.

Il-hyun reached out, smoothing a hand over Jakyeong’s hair. The strands felt remarkably soft against his fingers—a deep, rich brown mirroring the color of his eyes.

"Pay no mind to what Chairman Kang said."

"I don't. It's not as if I fully trust you either, Director Kang."

The hand resting on his hair drifted slowly downward, fingers tracing the crimson silk of the necktie.

"How cruel... after we've already shared a bed. Would sleeping together one more time earn a little trust?"

"I highly doubt that's on the table. Get some rest—I'm turning in."

Jakyeong offered a dry, dismissive smile and turned on his heel. But the moment his hand hit the doorknob, Il-hyun caught the handle from behind, slamming the door shut with a solid thud.

Jakyeong let out a quiet, tired sigh, his brow furrowing as he turned around. Il-hyun stepped flush against him, crowding his space.

"Care to join me for a swim?"

Jakyeong stared at him with sheer incredulity. He wanted to ask if the man had entirely lost his mind. Going for a swim in a torrential downpour where you couldn't see ten feet ahead? With lightning ripping through the sky? There was an old saying that thunder struck the wicked, but Kang Il-hyun apparently didn't fear acts of God in the slightest.

"Can you not see the weather outside?"

Il-hyun glanced toward the dark window, answering with complete nonchalance. "Looks lovely to me. Don't you like swimming in the rain?"

"Enjoy it to your heart's content, Director Kang... I'll pass."

"How about a pot of tea in my suite, then? I have a blend with a remarkably deep aroma."

"I'll pass on that, too."

"Then what about some target practice in the basement range?"

Jakyeong was on the verge of flatly rejecting that as well when he paused. His muscles were stiff from lying around, and blowing off steam sounded appealing; the mention of live fire set a familiar spark in his eyes.

Catching the subtle shift in interest, Il-hyun took a half-step back. "Go wash up, change into something comfortable, and meet me downstairs."

With that, he retreated down the hall without pressing further.

Jakyeong exhaled a long breath. It was still too early to sleep anyway; running a few magazines through a target seemed like an effective way to work out the tension.

Watching Il-hyun press his thumb to the private elevator scanner, Jakyeong recalled the biometric silicone gloves he’d obtained through Wang Ryun. Swapping the USB drive had gone so smoothly that he hadn't needed to lift the print, but he had kept the kit tucked away just in case.

Reaching the subterranean level, they stepped into the private firing range.

The facility was far more extensive than it appeared from the outside. While Jakyeong was taking in the acoustic baffling and automated target tracks, Il-hyun pressed a concealed panel on the concrete wall. The partition slid back, revealing a walk-in armory that made Jakyeong stop in his tracks.

He had expected a few handguns, but the reinforced vault held a full-scale tactical arsenal: rows of Glocks, Berettas, custom revolvers, tactical shotguns, precision sniper platforms, and even heavy anti-materiel rifles lining the racks.

Admiring the inventory, Jakyeong stepped closer, his eyes gleaming.

Watching the reaction, Il-hyun let out a wry chuckle. "It seems I rank lower on your priority list than a rack of firearms."

Ignoring the quip, Jakyeong pulled a tactical rifle from the rack, ran a quick slide-check, and seated a loaded magazine. Bracing the buttstock against his shoulder pocket, he snapped the muzzle around, locking the iron sights dead-center onto Kang Il-hyun’s face as the man leaned casually against the door frame.

Jakyeong pulled the trigger on the empty chamber with a dry snap.

Il-hyun clutched his chest in theatrical agony, groaning as if mortally wounded.

Jakyeong lowered the rifle, unimpressed by the performance. "If a real round hit you there, you wouldn't even manage a groan."

"I suppose I'll find out when the time comes."

Returning the rifle, Jakyeong continued browsing until he spotted a .38-caliber revolver with an intricate viper engraved along the pearl grip panel.

"A gift from my father," Il-hyun remarked.

"Quite striking. Are you fond of snakes, Director Kang?"

"Not particularly. I prefer dragons."

A serpent can never become a dragon. Perhaps Chairman Kang had gifted the piece as a subtle reminder of his illegitimate status.

"Take a few shots," Il-hyun offered.

Jakyeong turned toward the lane target, slotted six rounds into the cylinder, and pulled the hammer back with a clean metallic click.

Il-hyun stepped up close behind his shoulder, his hips resting lightly against Jakyeong’s rear as he leaned in, whispering against his ear:

"Picture someone you despise."

Jakyeong leveled his stance, aligned the front sight post, and squeezed the trigger.

Crack. Crack. Crack.

Six consecutive rounds punched a tight, ragged grouping dead-center between the target dummy's thighs.

Il-hyun’s eyes narrowed slightly.

Dissatisfied with just one cylinder, Jakyeong used a speedloader to seat six more rounds, rapidly emptying them into the exact same groin zone until the paper was completely pulverized into confetti.

Il-hyun let out a dry, strained chuckle. "Surely... you weren't picturing me just now?"

Jakyeong reached for another speedloader without offering a single word, prompting Il-hyun to catch the cylinder with his palm.

"That's enough. Put it away. Watching you ventilate that specific area is starting to make me physically ache."

Taking the revolver from his hands, Il-hyun returned it to the rack and hit the lock switch.

Jakyeong scowled in disappointment. He’d half-wanted to pull an LMG from the wall and imagine spraying down Kang Il-hyun's smug face, but the fun was cut short. Why bring me down here if you're going to shut it down after two cylinders?

Heading back toward the elevator, Il-hyun caught his elbow, guiding him down an adjacent corridor instead. The memory of getting drugged in the basement vault flared up, making Jakyeong plant his feet.

"Where are you taking me now?"

"Since we're down here, let's catch a movie."

"I'm tired. I want to go up."

"Don't be difficult. It's a full-sized theater bed—you can fall asleep while watching."

Tugging him along, they turned the corner into a private screening room. Outfitted with a wall-sized projection screen, a sprawling sectional lounger, a beverage bar, and a dedicated wine cellar, it was practically a commercial theater.

"What genre do you prefer?"

If he had a choice, Jakyeong secretly preferred a good romance.

"Romance is out of the question, obviously," Il-hyun mused, browsing the media server. "War? Sci-fi? Thriller? Horror?"

Such a limited imagination. Just because a man killed for a living didn't mean he exclusively consumed violence on screen.

When Jakyeong offered no preference, Il-hyun selected a domestic crime thriller with an unfamiliar title. Jakyeong stood awkwardly by the door until Il-hyun caught his wrist, pulling him onto the plush lounger.

The film was a gory psychological thriller, opening with a flurry of severed limbs, deep lacerations, and chaotic knife fights. On screen, a protagonist drove a hunting blade clean into an antagonist's midsection.

Watching the sequence, Jakyeong and Il-hyun shook their heads almost in unison.

"That's completely absurd," Il-hyun muttered.

"Who grips a combat blade like that...?" Jakyeong scoffed.

"And why butcher the torso at that angle? The man doesn't understand basic anatomy."

"Exactly. The rib cage is going to catch the edge on the back-stroke."

"Fuck's sake. Did they do zero technical research before shooting this garbage?"

Jakyeong found himself nodding in agreement. The choreography was an absolute mess.

"The director ought to be ashamed," Jakyeong remarked. "If I were the executive producer on this, I'd have put a bullet in him out of pure rage."

Il-hyun turned away from the screen, fixing a long, loaded look on Jakyeong.

"What?" Jakyeong asked.

"How did you know?"

"Know what?"

"One of our corporate subsidiaries handles media production and talent management," Il-hyun said, his tone turning remarkably dry. "That disaster on screen was the very first feature film we funded... and it bombed so hard it nearly tanked the division. I genuinely considered burying that director in a foundation trench."

Knowing full well how atrocious it was, why pick this specific movie to watch together?

Jakyeong opened his mouth, thought better of it, and clamped it shut. He had momentarily forgotten that Haewon Group was an octopus-like conglomerate spanning international logistics, heavy construction, retail distribution, luxury hospitality, and entertainment.

Still, watching the butchery on screen made it glaringly obvious why the film had been a box-office disaster. Given Il-hyun's temper, the fact that the director had survived the premiere was a miracle in itself.

Ultimately, they didn't even make it halfway through before Il-hyun killed the projector.
